transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-23 10:00 PDT | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Jordan, Samira (Redwood); Carlos, Priya (Novapay)

00:00 Jordan: okay hi everyone thanks for hopping on, um, quick agenda — recap last week, bench updates, decisions on streaming, and next steps.
00:08 Carlos: yeah thanks, we got pulled into infra stuff earlier, so appreciate squeezing this in.
00:12 Samira: no problem. I pulled the latest microbench results into the sheet I shared, link in chat. Note, transcription may mess up some model names.
00:22 Priya: got it, I have the sample traces ready but need to filter PII before upload.
00:28 Jordan: great, timeline for that?
00:30 Priya: by end of Friday, we think.
00:33 Jordan: perfect. Quick remind — goal this week was TTFT under 120ms for 512 tokens median and 95th under 250ms for our target model variant.
00:44 Samira: right. So, I ran three sets: baseline (no streaming), streaming with chunk_size 128, and streaming with chunk_size 256. Also compared kernel builds: default fused-attn vs alternative kernel (labeled k2 in the sheet).
00:58 Carlos: and quantization? did you keep int8?
01:02 Samira: yes int8 symmetric for these runs, with KV cache resident on GPU, no CPU offload.
01:08 Priya: curious why you didn't try CPU offload — our infra prefers to keep GPU for other tasks.
01:13 Samira: we measured CPU offload earlier, it added unpredictable jitter to TTFT because of PCIe copy times when cache miss patterns are bursty. For median it's okay but tail suffers.
01:25 Jordan: can you summarize numbers?
01:27 Samira: median TTFT baseline was ~170ms, streaming 128 dropped median to ~110ms, streaming 256 got ~125ms median but lower total tokens cost. 95th: baseline ~420ms, streaming128 ~230ms, streaming256 ~260ms. Kernel k2 improved 95th by ~10% across both streaming configs — basically smoother tail.
01:52 Carlos: so streaming128 hits our 120ms median target but costs more due to slightly higher request overhead?
01:59 Samira: correct. Chunk 128 means more requests and less effective batching, so per-token compute goes up a bit. But prefix KV cache reuse still helps.
02:08 Priya: what's the request pattern? We have many short prompts but occasional very long sessions (8k–16k). Are these numbers accounting for long-run KV warmup?
02:17 Samira: these microbenches used synthetic seq lengths matching your provided 90th/99th percentiles but not yet the very long 16k sessions — we need your traces for that. Initial extrapolation shows that with 8k sequences, k2 + streaming128 keeps 95th under ~350ms but we should run actual runs.
02:33 Jordan: remind me: TTFT here includes tokenizer and first decode?
02:36 Samira: yes from request ingress to first token emitted, including model forward and decode. Tokenization cost is minor on our infra.
02:43 Carlos: how about kernel choices — k2 is what? small-fused-attn variant?
02:46 Samira: k2 is a newer attention kernel tuned for long kv cache access patterns, slightly more memory but better locality. It trades off a bit on short sequences but helps tail on long seqs.
02:57 Priya: any quantization differences? Int8 is okay, but do we risk quality regression on edge cases?
03:02 Samira: we ran a quick eval on your eval set and quality delta was negligible; we can run more targeted evals on long-form prompts once you upload traces.
03:12 Jordan: there's also a routing option where we serve long sessions on dedicated nodes with higher memory and keep short on hosted. That avoids tail impact for the rest of traffic.
03:22 Carlos: cost? Would that require two SKUs?
03:24 Jordan: you'd have a mixed routing policy — short traffic to shared/hosted (cheaper), long sessions to reserved dedicated pool. We can show math. We'll send pricing.
03:33 Priya: the infra team would prefer dedicated for compliance but budget might be tight. Can we do a canary?
03:38 Samira: yes, canary routing is supported — 10% of long sessions to dedicated first, then scale. Also autoscale rules can be tuned for bursty long sessions.
03:47 Jordan: back to tuning — Samira, did you try tensor-slicing kernels or NVLink-enabled multi-GPU for 16k?
03:53 Samira: not yet. For 16k we'd need sequence-parallel or tensor-slicing across GPUs; that adds complexity but reduces latency growth. I recommend first running single-GPU with k2 and streaming to see real numbers, then if tail still bad, explore multi-GPU slicing.
04:10 Carlos: do you have rough cost delta for tensor-slicing?
04:13 Samira: it's higher — you pay for multiple GPUs active per request, but with big sessions it's sometimes necessary. We'll put rough cost per token numbers in the pricing note.
04:23 Priya: regarding streaming chunk size, is chunk 128 safe for our safety pipeline? We post-process tokens in near real-time.
04:30 Samira: yes we stream tokens as they're produced; your post-proc should tolerate partial outputs. If not, we can buffer a small lookahead.
04:38 Jordan: any misc notes from last week? Carlos you mentioned a flaky PCIe on one of your nodes — did that get resolved?
04:43 Carlos: infra team swapped the NIC, seemed better but still want to watch. That's why deterministic dedicated looks appealing.
04:49 Samira: okay, concrete plan: we run 8k and 16k benches with k2 + streaming128 and streaming256, capture TTFT median/95/99, and tail CPU/GPU utilization. Also try a run with CPU offload to demonstrate jitter.
05:04 Priya: yes please. We'll provide traces Friday and would like the bench results early next week.
05:09 Jordan: I'll schedule the benchmark review for Tue 06/29.
05:13 Carlos: and Jordan, send pricing for dedicated 4xA100 pool and the mixed routing example.
05:17 Jordan: will do. Anything else?
05:19 Priya: quick safety note — make sure logs don't contain raw cardholder data during traces; I'll scrub before upload.
05:25 Samira: understood. We'll only use anonymized traces and run in an isolated bench account.
05:30 Jordan: great, thanks everyone. We'll recap action items in email.
05:33 Carlos: thanks, talk soon.
05:35 Meeting end.
